mentions.name: Alaska
mentions.description: A serverless compute platform built from scratch without Kubernetes or existing orchestration layers, capable of spinning up dozens of containers in parallel in seconds. It emphasizes a fast feedback loop for writing code locally, testing instantly, and running remotely with minimal friction. A Python SDK uses decorators so local functions become distributed services without boilerplate, and a custom FUSE filesystem synchronizes code, data, and runtime across nodes. A beta is planned.
mentions.audience: Developers building and deploying distributed services
mentions.source_excerpt: I’m working on Alaska, a serverless compute platform I built entirely from scratch — no Kubernetes, no existing orchestration layers. It can spin up dozens of containers in parallel in just a few seconds.
